title: See Neuschwanstein from the Marienbrucke
description: Ludwig II's fantasy castle, unfinished when he died in 1886. The bridge over the gorge gives the view; the castle itself is timed-entry only.

title: Surf the standing wave on the Eisbach
description: A permanent river wave in the middle of the Englischer Garten, surfed around the clock and in the snow. Watching is free.

title: Drink in a Munich beer garden under the chestnuts
description: By Bavarian law you may bring your own food to a traditional beer garden and buy only the beer. The chestnut trees were planted to keep cellars cool.

title: Watch the Glockenspiel figures turn at Marienplatz
description: Forty-three bells and thirty-two figures re-enacting a 1568 wedding, at eleven and noon. It is gloriously slow.

title: Take the boat across the Konigssee
description: Electric boats only since 1909, so the lake is silent. The boatman stops halfway to play a trumpet at the cliff for the echo.

title: Ride up to the Eagle's Nest
description: A brass lift bored 124 metres up through the mountain to a Nazi-era teahouse, now a restaurant with an uneasy view.

title: Walk the Partnach Gorge
description: Seven hundred metres of tunnel and ledge cut through a gorge eighty metres deep. In winter it freezes into ice curtains.

title: Stand on the Zugspitze summit
description: Germany's highest point at 2,962 metres, reached by cable car or cog railway, with four countries visible on a clear day.

title: Walk the walls of Rothenburg ob der Tauber
description: A complete medieval walled town on the Romantic Road, with a covered walkway running most of the circuit.

title: Eat Nuremberg bratwurst three to a roll
description: Protected by law at seven to nine centimetres, grilled over beechwood and served three in a bun by street windows.

title: Walk the treetop canopy trail in the Bavarian Forest
description: A 1,300-metre walkway through the crowns of Germany's oldest national park, spiralling up a tower at the end.

title: Find the Wieskirche in a meadow
description: A rococo pilgrimage church standing alone in a field, so ornate inside that the plain exterior reads as a joke.

title: Go up the Reichstag dome
description: Foster's glass dome lets you look down into the parliament chamber below. Free, but you must register in advance.

title: Walk through the Holocaust memorial's stelae
place: Denkmal fur die ermordeten Juden Europas
description: Two thousand seven hundred and eleven concrete blocks on uneven ground. The information centre underneath is the harder half.

title: See the bust of Nefertiti on Museum Island
description: Five museums on one island in the Spree, including the Pergamon altar and a 3,300-year-old queen who needs no introduction.

title: Look for traces of the wall at the Mauerpark flea market
description: The death strip is now a Sunday flea market with open-air karaoke in the amphitheatre, which says most of what needs saying.

title: Swim in a lake inside the city at Wannsee
description: A 1,275-metre lido open since 1907, at the end of an S-Bahn line, and busy with Berliners rather than visitors.

title: See the Green Vault treasury in Dresden
description: August the Strong's treasure chamber, rebuilt after the firestorm. Timed entry to the historic rooms is capped at a hundred people an hour.

title: Hear Bach where he worked at the Thomaskirche
description: He was cantor here for twenty-seven years and is buried in the chancel. The boys' choir still sings the motet on Fridays.

title: Walk from Goethe's house to Buchenwald
description: Eight kilometres between the high point of German humanism and a concentration camp. Doing both in one day is the point.

title: See the Bauhaus building where modernism started
description: Gropius's 1926 school building, with the glass curtain wall that every office block since has borrowed from.

title: Punt the Spreewald canals
description: Two hundred channels through alder forest where the post is still delivered by boat, in the Sorbian-speaking corner of Germany.

title: Walk under the chalk cliffs at Jasmund
description: White cliffs above beech forest on the Baltic, painted by Caspar David Friedrich and protected as world heritage.

title: Watch cranes gather at the Muritz lakes
description: Tens of thousands of common cranes stage here each autumn before flying south. Dawn and dusk from the hides.

title: Climb the south tower of Cologne Cathedral
description: Five hundred and thirty-three steps up the tallest twin-spired church in the world, which took 632 years to finish.

title: Tour the Zollverein coal mine
description: The most beautiful coal mine in the world by its own reckoning, closed in 1986 and now world heritage, with a swimming pool in the coking plant.

title: Hear a concert in the Elbphilharmonie
description: A glass wave dropped on a brick warehouse, with a hall tuned by Yasuhisa Toyota. The public plaza halfway up is free.

title: Walk the Speicherstadt warehouse canals
description: The largest warehouse district in the world, on oak piles in the water, best at night when the brick is floodlit.

title: Get up early for the Fischmarkt
description: Sunday from five in the morning, half fish market and half the end of Saturday night, with a brass band in the auction hall.

title: Walk the Wadden Sea mudflats at low tide
description: A guided wattwanderung across the seabed to an island. The tide comes back faster than you can walk, so do not go alone.

title: Eat marzipan in Lubeck
description: The Hanseatic capital, with a brick gothic gate that is sinking, and the marzipan house that has been at it since 1806.

title: Walk the Rote Kliff on Sylt
description: Forty kilometres of North Sea beach on a thin island reached by a causeway train, with red cliffs at Kampen.

title: Ride the Schwarzwaldbahn through the Black Forest
description: Thirty-nine tunnels and a full spiral to gain height, engineered in the 1860s and still the scenic way across.

title: Walk to the Triberg waterfalls
description: Germany's best-known falls drop 163 metres in seven steps, through forest full of red squirrels that expect to be fed.

title: Cycle around Lake Constance
description: Two hundred and sixty kilometres through three countries on a signed lakeside route, with ferries to cut corners.

title: Walk the Philosophers' Way above Heidelberg
description: A steep path up the far bank with the ruined castle and the old bridge below. Hegel and Holderlin walked it, hence the name.

title: Walk the Calmont via ferrata above the Moselle
description: The steepest vineyard in Europe at 65 degrees, with ladders and cables bolted through it above a bend in the river.

title: Drink apfelwein in Sachsenhausen
description: Served from a grey stoneware bembel into ribbed glasses in taverns that hang a pine wreath out when the new batch is ready.
